siblingApproaches.approach: Start at the Rachel Lake Trailhead (Trail #1313, elev. ~2,800 ft) at the end of Box Canyon Road/FR-4930. Follow the Rachel Lake Trail as it climbs gently through forest along the Box Canyon Creek drainage — the grade is easy and well-graded here, mostly Class 1 hiking. siblingTrailheads.trailhead: Dingford Creek Trailhead (Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From I-90 exit 34 near North Bend, follow 468th to Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road, turn right and drive 12 miles, passing the large Middle Fork parking area on the right. Cross the large concrete bridge, immediately turn right onto the gravel road signed for Dingford and Dutch Miller Gap, and follow it about 6 miles to the gate and trailhead.

siblingApproaches.approach: Drive the Middle Fork Snoqualmie Road (FR 56) to the Dingford Creek Trailhead (~1,400 ft). Hike the Dingford Creek Trail, crossing several creeks, toward the Hester Lake basin (roughly 5-6 miles) before leaving the trail to begin the off-trail scramble.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the pullout along FR 6835 (West Fork Foss Road) — just past the concrete bridge over the East Fork Foss River, about half a mile from its junction with FR 68 and roughly 5.2 miles from US-2 at Skykomish — there is no maintained trail. Climbers cross to the north side of the road and pick up the toe of Bald Eagle's north ridge at about 1,600 ft, entering second-growth forest thick with fallen timber that requires weaving/scrambling over deadfall for the first few hundred feet of gain. siblingTrailheads.trailhead: North Fork Sauk Trailhead (FR-49, Sloan Creek Road)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Darrington, south on the Mountain Loop Highway about 16 miles to Sloan Creek Road (FR-49), then east on FR-49 about 6.6 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead (~2,100 ft).

siblingApproaches.approach: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead (off Sloan Creek Road, FR 49), follow North Fork Sauk Trail #649 up the valley through old-growth forest, past the Red Creek bridge to Mackinaw Shelter, then up a long series of switchbacks to meet the Pacific Crest Trail at about 5,950 ft, roughly 8-9 miles from the car. White Pass and its camp are a short way south along the PCT; this route does not go there. Turn north on the PCT and cross Red Pass (about 6,500 ft) a mile or two on, then descend into the upper White Chuck valley and follow the PCT down it for roughly 7-9 miles, past the old White Chu

siblingApproaches.route: Disappointment Peak Cleaver (Gerdine Ridge / Cool Glacier)
siblingApproaches.approach: From the North Fork Sauk River Trailhead (2,050 ft, off FR 49/Sloan Creek Road), hike ~9 mi to White Pass on the PCT. Continue east on the Foam Creek Trail ~2 mi, cross a ridge saddle near 6,600 ft, then traverse the White Chuck Glacier basin trending NE to Glacier Gap (~7,300 ft), the standard high camp where the Suiattle and White Chuck glaciers meet. Summit day is roughly 7 mi round trip with about 3,450 ft of gain, some of it height lost and regained along the way: climb gentle snow above camp, follow a climber's track on volcanic scree onto the Gerdine and Cool glaciers, end-run a crevass

siblingTrailheads.trailhead: PCT Trailhead, Snoqualmie Pass (Exit 52, Alpental Rd)
siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From I-90 take Exit 52; the trailhead is at the end of the gravel ski-area parking lot, reached by turning left under the freeway and taking the first right from the eastbound off-ramp, or by turning right and immediately right again from the westbound off-ramp.

siblingApproaches.approach: Park at the PCT North Trailhead at Snoqualmie Pass (I-90 Exit 52, large lot off SR 906/Alpental Rd; Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass required). Head north on the Pacific Crest Trail; most parties cut the corner via the Commonwealth Basin/Red Pass climbers' shortcut, which rejoins the PCT and trims about a mile off the standard trail. siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From the Stuart Lake/Colchuck Lake Trailhead (~3,500 ft, end of Eightmile Road/FR-7601)

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Stuart Lake/Colchuck Lake Trailhead (~3,500 ft, end of Eightmile Road/FR-7601), follow the Stuart Lake Trail (#1599) about 2.5 miles to the signed fork where the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599.1) splits left/south. Continue roughly 1.8 more miles — crossing Mountaineer Creek and a boulder-hop stretch near the outlet — to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft, ~4.3 mi in), the last easy, reliable water before the pass. Skirt the lake's south/east shoreline on a braided, cairned climbers' path over talus and slab to the base of Aasgard Pass, the obvious steep gully/headwall at the lake's south end. Aasga
